items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: Well he was Marty Two, I was Marty One, and Shelly was the drummer

ctx.x: I guess so. You know it might have been an advantage for you that he didn’t get to the piano part, because he might have written something very difficult, if you weren’t a reader at the time.

Well actually what happened was he would pass out the parts at the rehearsals see, and the bass player’s name was Marty too. See? Well he was Marty Two, I was Marty One, and Shelly was the drummer, and he would give us blank manuscripts and he would say “Shelly, Marty Bass and Marty Piano.” The only reason we knew it was piano was because in the left hand side it said “Piano,” and the manuscript was empty. And I’d say “hey Neal, when are you going to write me a part? I’m trying to learn how to read music.” So…

with comedians and dancers, I was lucky that we had an 18 piece orchestra. And fortunately I had what they called a piano/conductor part. And on the top, in red ink, was what the lead trumpet was playing, see? So now I would fake through the first show and from the second show on I would follow the red notes on the piano sheets see? And I would notice like whenever the band had an eighth rest and a dotted quarter, I know it always went [scats] and I said, hey that’s great, you know. By the time I left that band I…
